output.summary: The incident rise is best explained by a self-reinforcing loop. Interrupt load displaced reliability work, overdue postmortem action items accumulated, and known failure modes recurred (60% of Q3 SEV1-SEV2). Storage's exemption is a natural experiment: it closed its backlog and its incidents fell while its traffic share stayed flat. Volume growth (+7%), the tool migration (which never touches SEV1-SEV2) and coverage gaps (the Networking pilot, acknowledgment times) do not explain it. The hiring freeze worsened on-call frequency but did not start the rise. Attrition mixes pay and on-call, so the cause is unresolved. A second primary slot would push on-call to about 1 week in 3 and accelerate attrition. Ring-fencing engineers to clear recurring-incident fixes is the best next step. Incident-count targets risk repeating the 2023 under-reporting.
